Issue:
Enumeration Types are not usable in templates.
Description
	 
		(last modified by Mariusz Felisiak)
	 
The new ​enumeration types are great but can't be used in Django templates due to their being callable. For example this doesn't work:
{% if student.year_in_school == YearInSchool.FRESHMAN %}
This is because YearInSchool, being a class, is callable, and Django Templates always call callables with no arguments. The call fails because the required value argument is missing.
The easy solution would be to declare do_not_call_in_templates = True on the various Choices classes.

Required files:
django/db/models/enums.py

tool_arguments.summary: The root cause of the issue is that the enumeration classes defined in `django/db/models/enums.py` are callable, and Django templates automatically call callables without arguments. This leads to a failure when trying to use the enumeration types in templates. The expected behavior is that the enumeration types should be usable in templates without being called. To resolve this issue, the `do_not_call_in_templates = True` attribute should be added to the `Choices`, `IntegerChoices`, and `TextChoices` classes. This will prevent Django templates from calling these classes, allowing them to be used correctly in template logic.
